players.name: Jamie Carragher
players.note: The season he became a centre-back for good, and immediately the best defender in a European Cup-winning side. A real step up rather than drift.

players.name: Steven Gerrard
players.note: Captain of a European Cup-winning side and the driving force of it; a rung below the Lampard anchor (90) on league-long consistency, Liverpool having finished fifth.

players.name: Luis García
players.note: Technically the best of Liverpool’s attacking players that season and decisive in Europe; erratic week to week, which is what keeps him out of the elite band.

players.name: Milan Baroš
players.note: The Euro 2004 golden boot season carried into a genuinely sharper year: elite acceleration and a much improved first touch, still a narrow all-round game.

players.name: Xabi Alonso
players.note: A broken ankle in January cost him half the season; before and after it he was already one of the best long passers in the league at 22.

players.name: Harry Kewell
players.note: Chronic groin trouble reduced him to fifteen starts; he was never the same athlete afterwards.

players.name: Fernando Morientes
players.note: The Liverpool spell was a failure, but this is a Real Madrid and Monaco centre-forward, a Spain international who had led the Champions League scoring the season before. Rated on the footballer, not the three goals.

players.name: Mauricio Pellegrino
players.note: Arrived from a La Liga title win at thirty-two and was plainly too slow for England; an intelligent, well-drilled defender whose legs had gone.

players.name: Stephen Warnock
players.note: A genuine Premier League left-back - fit, sound defensively, limited going forward.

players.name: Djibril Cissé
players.note: The season was ended in October by a broken leg. Rated as the France international and twice Ligue 1 top scorer he was at twenty-two: frightening pace and a real finish, raw everywhere else.

players.name: Antonio Núñez
players.note: A makeweight in the Owen deal who never justified a Real Madrid squad number; no end product and little presence.

players.name: Neil Mellor
players.note: A penalty-box finisher with a handful of memorable goals in very few minutes; knee injuries stopped him before he could be judged higher.

players.name: Scott Carson
players.note: Nineteen; a big, athletic keeper with obvious raw material who went on to play for England.
